fields.soakHours: Hours to plan the soak for. soakRange holds the low and high ends the source allows.
fields.refreshEveryHours: Change still water this often. null means the source gives no schedule.
fields.incubateHours: Hours after draining to start checking for sprouts. incubateRange holds the earliest and latest the source allows, sowWhen says what ready looks like.
fields.seedKgPerHa: Seed in kg per hectare as a low and high pair, by planting method.
fields.transplantAgeDays: Seedling age at transplanting in days as a low and high pair.
fields.confidence: company means the seed company or breeder said it. general means no brand instruction was found and the PhilRice hybrid steps stand in.

howToMatch: Compare whole names, ignoring case, spaces and dashes, never a substring (Mestiso 1 must not match Mestiso 117). Walk brands in order and take the first whose match list holds the record name, its NSIC number or a trade name. Fall back to brandWords, then breeders, then general.hybrid or general.inbred by the record type. The US 88 entry sits before the wider SeedWorks entry on purpose.

inbred.label: Inbred certified seed (PhilRice PalayCheck and Pinoy Rice Knowledge Bank)
inbred.sowWhen: When the white root tip shows like a small dot on most seeds.
inbred.seedbed: About 400 square meters of raised seedbed per hectare, 1 meter wide and 4 to 5 cm high. Sow about 100 grams per square meter for certified seed.
steps: Put the seed in a clean, strong sack or net bag filled only halfway so it has room to swell.
Soak it for 24 hours in flowing water, or in a drum of clean water.
If the seed sits in a drum, change the water every 6 hours so it does not sour.
Lift the sack out and let it drain on a raised pallet in the shade.
Incubate for 24 to 36 hours under a cover, until the white root tip shows.
Do not stack the sacks. Heat builds up and can kill the sprouting seed.
Keep the seed damp and let air reach it until it is sown.
Sow the sprouted seed right away so the roots do not tangle.
inbred.directSeeded: Soak 24 hours and incubate 24 to 36 hours, then let the seed air dry a little so it spreads evenly. Use 40 to 60 kg per hectare with a drum seeder and 60 to 80 kg when broadcasting by hand.
inbred.notes: In the cool dry season incubation can take up to 48 hours. Some PhilRice guides give 12 to 24 hours of soaking for inbred seed.

hybrid.label: Hybrid seed with no brand instruction (PhilRice hybrid guidance)
hybrid.sowWhen: When white roots show on most seeds.
hybrid.seedbed: About 400 square meters of seedbed per hectare. Sow about 50 grams, one handful, per square meter.
steps: Wash the seed in a pail of clean water.
Put it in a sack or net bag that lets water through.
Soak it 12 to 24 hours in flowing water or in a drum of clean water.
Do not throw away seeds that float. Hybrid seed is often lighter, darker and slightly open, and these seeds still grow.
If the water is not flowing, change it every 6 hours so the seed does not ferment.
Wash the seed well after soaking and set the sack on a pallet or wooden platform.
Incubate 24 to 36 hours until white roots show.
Keep the seed damp while it incubates. Rinse it and turn the sacks every 4 to 6 hours so it does not overheat.
hybrid.directSeeded: No PhilRice hybrid rate for direct seeding was found. Brand guides use 15 to 36 kg per hectare, see the brand entries.
hybrid.notes: Older PhilRice guides give a shorter soak for hybrids: 10 to 12 hours in flowing water, or 12 hours with the water changed every 3 hours. Start checking for swollen seed at 12 hours.

irri.label: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank pregermination
irri.sowWhen: Root about 2 to 3 mm long. Sow before roots pass 5 mm.
steps: Soak the seed 12 to 24 hours, or until small shoots appear at the tip.
In cold weather the soak may need 36 to 48 hours.
Drain and keep the seed in its bag for about 24 hours in a shady place where air moves around the bags.
Do not let the bags get hotter than about 42 degrees Celsius or some seed will be damaged.
Broadcast or drum seed before the roots pass 5 mm. Longer roots tangle and break at sowing.
Weigh the seed dry. Soaking adds 10 to 30 percent to its weight.
irri.directSeeded: Wet direct seeding needs about 80 kg per hectare of an inbred suited to direct seeding. Pregerminated seed cannot go through a drill seeder.

rules.rule: Hybrid seed needs far less seed than inbred: about 15 to 18 kg per hectare transplanted, against 20 to 40 kg of certified inbred seed.
Never discard floating or half filled hybrid seed. Bayer, Longping and the Pioneer guide all say these seeds still grow, so a salt or float test is for inbred seed only.

Soak in a loose sack or net bag. Flowing water is best. In still water change it on a schedule, every 6 hours for most brands, every 4 to 6 for Longping, every 3 for SL Agritech, so the seed does not sour.

Incubate on a raised pallet in the shade, never on the floor and never with sacks stacked. Keep the seed damp and aired, and mix or turn it every 3 to 6 hours. Overheating sours and kills sprouting seed.
Sow when about 85 percent of the seed shows a white root. For direct seeding, sow before roots pass 5 mm.
Cool weather slows everything. IRRI allows 36 to 48 hours of soaking in cold weather and PhilRice up to 48 hours of incubation in the dry season.
A whole preparation takes about two to three days from first soak to sowing. Plan the seedbed or field to be ready on the day the seed is.

brands.sowWhen: When about 85 percent of the seed has opened and shows a white root.
brands.seedbed: 400 square meters of seedbed 4 to 5 cm high. Sow one handful per square meter.
steps: Put the seed in a sack that water passes through easily.
Wash the seed, then soak it for 12 hours.
Change to clean water every 3 hours. Seed left in old water sours and sprouts poorly.
Lift the sack and incubate for 24 to 36 hours, one to one and a half days, in a shaded place.
Keep the sack closed. Dip it in water for about 5 seconds every 3 to 5 hours so the seed stays damp and cool.
Do not let the seed overheat while it incubates. Too much heat sours and darkens the seed and can kill it.
Sow on the seedbed once about 85 percent of the seed has cracked open with a white root.
brands.directSeeded: Use 30 to 36 kg per hectare when broadcasting, against 15 to 18 kg when transplanting.
brands.notes: From the SL Agritech planting guide animation (five steps for sprouting SL hybrid seed), shown re uploaded with credit to SL Agritech. SL says every pack carries the same printed guide. It matches the owner note of about 12 hours.

brands.sowWhen: When more than 85 percent of the seed has sprouted.
brands.seedbed: One 3 kg pack covers 1,800 to 2,000 square meters of field. Keep the seedbed wet for 5 to 7 days after sowing, then hold 1 to 2 cm of water.
steps: Plan 15 to 18 kg per hectare, which is 5 to 6 packs of 3 kg.
Put each 3 kg of seed in its own net bag or sack.
Soak each bag in a drum or pail of clean water for 18 to 24 hours.
Do not throw away seeds that float. They also sprout.
Change the water every 4 to 6 hours, and wash the seed at each change so it does not sour or rot.
After 18 to 24 hours lift the bags onto a pallet or rack so the water drains. Never set them on the bare floor.
Incubate for 24 to 36 hours or a little longer, covered with a tarp.
Mix the seed every 5 to 6 hours, and sprinkle or pour clean water on it so it does not overheat or sour.
Sow on the seedbed once more than 85 percent of the seed has sprouted.
brands.directSeeded: No Longping direct seeding rate was found.
brands.notes: Owner note says about 24 hours with the water drained and renewed every 6 hours, which fits the official video. The 2021 Longping technical training deck gives the same steps and adds transplanting at 18 to 20 days, 1 to 2 seedlings a hill at 20 by 20 cm.

brands.sowWhen: When the root emerges, seen as white dots or a swollen embryo.
brands.seedbed: 300 to 400 square meters of wet bed for 15 kg, raised 5 to 10 cm and about 1 meter wide with 40 cm drains. Sow 3 kg on 60 to 80 square meters.
steps: Plan 15 kg per hectare, which is 5 packs of 3 kg.
Soak the seed 18 to 24 hours in clean water.
If the water is not flowing, change it every 6 hours.
Do not discard floating or half filled seeds.
Make sure the seed has taken up enough water, then drain it.
Incubate 24 to 48 hours until the root emerges. Keep the seed moist and aired and cover it.
Do not pile the sacks on each other, and turn the seed over gradually so heat does not build up.
Sow when white dots or a swollen embryo show.
brands.directSeeded: Bayer says Arize can be transplanted or direct seeded, but gives no direct seeding rate on its Philippine pages.
brands.notes: Transplant at the 3 to 5 leaf stage, which is 21 to 23 days after sowing for AZ 8433 DT, 1 to 2 seedlings a hill at 20 by 20 cm. Keep the seedbed saturated 5 to 7 days after sowing, then raise water to 1 to 2 cm. Bigante and Bigante Plus are Bayer Arize hybrids, not Bioseed.

brands.seedbed: 300 to 400 square meters of seedbed. Sow 50 grams per square meter and keep 2 to 3 cm of water once seedlings stand.
steps: Put the seed in a sack.
Wash it and soak it in water for 12 to 24 hours, or until the seed has swelled.
Do not throw away seeds that float.
Change the water every 6 hours unless it is flowing.
Lift the seed out of the water and wash it.
Incubate 24 to 36 hours. Turn the sack over again and again while it incubates.
Keep the seed warm but not hot.
Sow when white roots show.
brands.directSeeded: For drum seeding Pioneer used 15 to 20 kg of PHB71 per hectare, soaked 12 to 24 hours and incubated 12 to 36 hours.
brands.notes: The older Pioneer planting guide reprinted by ATI gives incubation of 12 to 36 hours. The newer Corteva film gives 24 to 36.

brands.seedbed: Sow about 50 grams, one handful, per square meter.
steps: Plan 15 kg per hectare for transplanting and split it into three clean sacks of 5 kg.
Soak US 88 longer than other hybrids, 36 to 48 hours.
Incubate 24 to 36 hours under a cover.
Keep the seed damp and never let it dry out.
Sow the sprouted seed on the seedbed at one handful per square meter.
brands.directSeeded: For broadcasting use 25 to 30 kg per hectare, split into 3 portions of 8 to 10 kg so the field is covered evenly.
brands.notes: SeedWorks shows no water change schedule. Changing the water every 6 hours, as PhilRice advises for still water, is a safe addition over a soak this long.

brands.brand: SeedWorks US Agriseeds (TH 82, Quadro Alas and other lines)
brands.seedbed: Sow about 50 grams, one handful, per square meter.
steps: Plan 15 kg per hectare for transplanting and split it into three clean sacks of 5 kg.
Soak the seed 12 to 24 hours.
Incubate 24 to 36 hours under a cover.
Keep the seed damp and never let it dry out.
Sow the sprouted seed on the seedbed at one handful per square meter.
brands.directSeeded: For broadcasting use 25 to 30 kg per hectare, split into 3 portions of 8 to 10 kg.
brands.notes: SeedWorks shows no water change schedule. Change still water every 6 hours as PhilRice advises.

brands.notes: No seed preparation instruction from Leads Agri was found online. These are the PhilRice hybrid steps. Jackpot 102 is NSIC Rc 666H.

brands.seedbed: 400 square meters of seedbed 1 meter wide with 10 to 15 bags of organic matter worked in. Sow 50 grams, about one handful, per square meter. Keep 1 to 2 cm of water once seedlings grow.
steps: Use new seed, 15 to 18 kg per hectare.
Soak 12 to 24 hours in flowing clean water.
If the water is not flowing, change it every 6 hours.
Wash the seed well after soaking and set it on wood or a pallet.
Incubate 24 to 36 hours until roots sprout.
Do not worry if the seed looks darker, lighter, thinner or slightly open. That is normal for hybrid seed.
brands.directSeeded: No PhilRice direct seeding rate for its hybrids was found.
brands.notes: Transplant 18 to 21 day seedlings, 1 to 2 per hill, only 2 to 3 cm deep. The word Mestiso alone is the NSIC local name of every registered hybrid, so match on the full name with its number, never the bare word.
